reading.body:
CyrusOne's Florence, Kentucky campus publishes 5 MW of IT capacity across 143,000 square feet of technical space, more than half of Kentucky's total published data center capacity.

Kentucky has three data centers with published power figures, totaling 9.55 MW, and five mapped facilities overall. Most mapped facilities publish no power specification at all, so 9.55 MW is a floor rather than a census of what is installed. By published capacity the state is a small node in the US data center footprint, and nothing in these figures marks it as a center of AI scaling.

At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 5 MW of IT load is roughly 125 racks. That is a small quantity for AI training, and the certification list, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and Green Globes, describes a facility built for regulated enterprise and cloud tenants rather than GPU workloads. The suitability score of 50, derived from published IT capacity and operator type, reflects the same reading, and the one input it lacks is announced expansion.

What the data does not cover is the part that would decide the question. It reports no grid capacity, no interconnection status, no power purchase arrangements, and no retrofit plans. Whether this campus becomes relevant to AI depends on decisions that published specifications do not contain.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
